subject: Confirm your Chase details
top_finding: A link points at a lookalike domain

message.subject: Confirm your Chase details
message.excerpt:
https://www.chase.com/account
 to confirm your password within 24 hours.

findings.title: A link points at a lookalike domain
evidence: Link to account-chase[.]example wraps the name from chase[.]com in extra words (imitating Chase)
findings.lesson: Hover before you click. The link's domain, not its text, tells you where you'll land.

findings.title: Sender domain imitates a known domain
evidence: Sender domain account-chase[.]example wraps the name from chase[.]com in extra words (imitating Chase)
findings.lesson: Read the domain letter by letter. Attackers register names that look right at a glance.

findings.title: Link text shows one site, link goes to another
evidence: Link reads "https://www.chase.com/account" but goes to account-chase[.]example
findings.lesson: What a link says and where it goes can differ. Hover to see the real destination before clicking.

findings.title: Display name poses as a brand
evidence: Display name "Chase" claims Chase, sent from account-chase[.]example
findings.lesson: The name on a message is free text. Check the address, not just who it says it is.

findings.title: Asks you to sign in, and fast
evidence: Wording asks for credentials under pressure: "confirm your password"; "within 24 hours"
findings.lesson: Pressure plus a login request is the classic pairing. Pause, then go to the site on your own.

contributions.label: Display name poses as a brand
